title: Metals and rust
examples: What is the difference between a metal and a non-metal?
Can you show me how rust forms on iron?
What is the best way to stop metal from rusting?

explain.say: Let us first look at some general properties of metals you might know.
Metals are usually shiny and they conduct electricity very well.
A key property is that metals are malleable and ductile materials.
Now we learn that rusting needs two things to happen together.
For example, if you leave iron nails out in wet air, they will rust.
One way to prevent rusting is by painting the metal surface.

faq.q: What exactly is rust made from?
faq.a: Rust is a form of iron oxide. It forms when iron reacts with oxygen in the presence of water.

faq.q: Does iron only rust in seawater?
faq.a: No, while seawater speeds it up, iron can rust in fresh water if oxygen is present.

faq.q: What is the best way to stop metal from rusting?
faq.a: The best methods involve coating the metal or removing oxygen or water.
asks: How do builders stop metal from rusting?

faq.a: Most common metals are shiny, but some metals can appear dull depending on their surface condition.
asks: Does dullness mean it is not a metal?

faq.q: Why is painting metal a good protection?
faq.a: Painting creates a barrier that keeps the water and oxygen away from the underlying metal.
asks: Does paint stop the chemical reaction?

facts: Metals are generally shiny and good conductors of heat.
Rusting is an oxidation process that requires both water and oxygen.
Painting or oiling metal surfaces helps prevent rusting by creating a barrier.
Malleability means a metal can be hammered into thin sheets.

quiz.say: Which property describes a metal that can be drawn into a thin wire?
quiz.why: Ductile specifically describes the ability to be drawn into a wire.

wrong.0: Malleable describes being hammered into sheets, not pulled into wires.
wrong.1: Conductive describes moving heat or electricity, not shape change.
wrong.2: Oxidised is a chemical change, not a physical property of the metal.

quiz.say: What must be present for iron to rust?
quiz.why: The process of rusting is an oxidation reaction that needs both water and oxygen to occur.

wrong.0: While acids can speed it up, the basic requirements are water and oxygen.
wrong.2: Water alone is not enough; oxygen is also needed for the chemical change.
wrong.3: Oxygen needs a liquid medium, like water, to react with the iron.

quiz.say: If you coat iron with grease, what are you doing to stop rusting?
quiz.why: Grease acts as a physical barrier, stopping water and oxygen from touching the iron.

wrong.0: You are not removing the iron; you are just protecting the existing metal.
wrong.2: The grease does not change the iron itself, it just covers it up.
wrong.3: While it protects it, the primary action is blocking the elements, not adding strength.
